references.text: The promise of a land flowing with milk and honey was first given to Moses at the burning bush, the same promise repeated here in Deuteronomy.
The description of the promised land as one flowing with milk and honey is repeated in connection with the exodus from Egypt.
The Lord promises to give the Israelites a land flowing with milk and honey, the same promise confirmed here.
The spies confirm that the land truly flows with milk and honey, just as the Lord had promised.
The exhortation to hear and keep the commandments so that it may go well with them, parallel to the promise of blessing through obedience.
The promise of long life in the land flowing with milk and honey, linked to obedience to God's commands.
The confession that the Lord brought the people into a land flowing with milk and honey, the fulfillment of the promise.
The prayer for blessing over the land flowing with milk and honey, which the Lord promised to the fathers.
The Lord confirms that he has brought the people into the land he swore to give their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.
The prophet Jeremiah describes Israel as a glorious land, an inheritance that is the finest of all nations, a parallel to the promise of the good land.
Ezekiel describes the promised land as the most glorious of all lands, a land flowing with milk and honey.
